Lemma
[$(\sqrt{|\cdot |})^{-1}$ is Smooth Away from the Origin]

For $t\in \mathbb R\setminus \{ 0\} $, the function $s\mapsto (\sqrt{|s|})^{-1}$ is smooth at $t$.

Proof

\sketch Near a positive $t$, $|s|=s$; near a negative $t$, $|s|=-s$. Compose this local linear expression with the smooth square-root function on $(0,\infty )$ and inversion on $\mathbb R\setminus \{ 0\} $.

□
